name: Living Ink
description: Plant a drop of ink. Watch it branch, follow a drawing, or remember an image.

assets.credit: Original simulated ink study · Tampa Curated
Original heron line drawing · Tampa Curated

compatibility: WebGL2 with floating-point framebuffer support runs two alternating GPU state textures. No third-party runtime packages.
If graphics are unsupported or interrupted, the same equations run on a smaller 160-cell-wide CPU grid. Graphics interruption starts a fresh field.
Pointer, touch, and keyboard seeds; reduced motion begins paused. Offscreen and hidden experiments stop advancing.
Image uploads accept PNG, JPEG and WebP up to 8 MB and 16 megapixels. They stay in this session and are never uploaded.
Still PNG export captures the current paper. Presets and source exports save the recipe, not the complete evolving state or a custom uploaded image.
notes: A Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion field stores two reacting concentrations, deposited pigment, and a memory of where the ink has travelled. Each new step depends on the last.
Architecture alters local reaction rates around a connected observatory drawing. The heron mask influences both chemistry and pigment: an untouched area cannot reveal its hidden image.

Five recipes explore branching roots, charcoal islands, sepia lace, growing architecture, and an image emerging from ink. Some parameter combinations deliberately fade or settle; reseed or choose a recipe to explore again.

Ink edges and hatching are rendered from the chemical field. There are no moving particles or prerecorded sequences. Changing resolution or mode begins a fresh field; other parameters act on the current ink.
reuse: Extract the source ZIP, serve it over local HTTP, and open example.html. No installation is needed.
For the complete instrument, import mount from index.js and pass a sized host element and settings. Call setRunning(true), then dispose() before removing it.
For your own interface, import createInkEngine from engine.js. Supply an RGBA mask or build one with pathMask or imageMask; send normalized brush inputs and call step() and render().
Read README.md for mask channels, equations, lifecycle, resource disposal, and portable usage. Preset JSON stores the recipe; read() exposes a numerical state snapshot.
